# School and college planning platforms competitive review

Research date: October 18, 2026. Scope: Naviance by PowerSchool, Xello, Scoir, Unifrog, MajorClarity by Edmentum, BigFuture, and Cialfo, with Appily, Niche, and CollegeVine as adjacent family-facing competitors.

The opportunity for a small, friendly parent/student guide is a useful first conversation followed by a few explainable options and a next action. Established platforms already connect self-discovery to career research and college planning. Competing by adding more questionnaires would weaken the intended experience. Short entry points and optional depth are defensible: Scoir documents an approximately five-minute interest assessment, Xello stages its assessment, and Unifrog explicitly advises against taking its full set in one sitting. Sources: [Scoir — Taking a career interest assessment](https://help.scoir.com/article/ss5linxlbo-taking-a-career-assessment), [Xello — Interests Assessments](https://help.xello.world/en-us/Content/Knowledge-Base/Xello-6-12/Assessments/Interests-Assessments.htm), [Unifrog — Psychometric testing FAQs](https://www.unifrog.org/help/unifrogs-psychometric-testing-faqs).

**Follow-up evidence update:** the later [student-outcomes review](./competitive-student-outcomes-2026-10-18.md.html) adds an August 2026 independent MDRC study, historical peer-reviewed Naviance decision studies, and checks of vendor outcome claims. Its bounded findings supersede first-pass statements below that independent outcomes were unverified.

## Evidence and comparison boundaries

This is a review of official public product pages, help documentation, policies, and vendor brochures. No accounts were created, purchases made, or real student data submitted. There was no authenticated student-session usability test. Consequently, “documented UX” describes published workflows, screenshots, and vendor compatibility statements; it is not a hands-on speed, accessibility, comprehension, or mobile-quality finding. Assessment times are vendor estimates, not measured times. A feature marked unverified may exist behind a school login or in another package.

Career-interest matching, self-reported skills, personality descriptions, assessed reasoning skills, college preference fit, and admission likelihood answer different questions. They should not be combined into one purported aptitude score. A named framework or a large occupation database does not, by itself, establish predictive validity for an individual teenager. The evidence below distinguishes disclosed inputs, user-visible explanations, content freshness, and validation claims.

## Naviance by PowerSchool

**Assessment and matching.** Naviance documents Holland-based Career Key and Career Interest Profiler. The broader menu includes Career Cluster Finder (108 questions/~20 minutes), AchieveWorks Personality (36 scenarios/~15), Intelligences (54/~15), Learning & Productivity (69/~20), Skills (69/~20), and StrengthsExplorer (78/~20; not retakable). These are separate school-assigned tools, not a documented mandatory intake battery. Other assessments can be resumed and generally retaken. [Self-Discovery](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance-student/latest/self-discovery).

College preference matching is especially instructive: SuperMatch lets students separate must-haves from nice-to-haves; results update as criteria change, and “Why?” displays a score breakdown. Academic comparisons use GPA/test-score averages. The documented explanation makes preference fit inspectable, but it does not establish an individualized admission probability. [College Planning in Naviance Student](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance/latest/college-planning-in-naviance-student).

**Breadth and actions.** Career profiles support salary/education sorting, interviews, non-degree training/certification profiles, and personalized insights, including AI-generated summaries. College tools include research, applications, and scholarships. Planner 2.0 assigns tasks by grade and selected path and shows deadlines, status, and completion. [Career Planning](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance-student/latest/career-planning), [College Planning](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance-student/latest/college-planning), [Planner 2.0](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance-student/latest/planner-2-0). A household lifestyle-cost simulator was not verified in the examined pages.

**UX and trust.** Published quick tips, optional criteria, and “Why?” are useful progressive-disclosure patterns. Actual mobile assessment usability remains untested. September 23, 2026 release notes identify Peterson’s as a college data provider and remove unsupported or stale fields, including a discontinued campus rating. That is concrete maintenance evidence, not a universal refresh schedule or calibration result. [College Planning in Naviance Student](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance/latest/college-planning-in-naviance-student), [Release notes 2026](https://ps.powerschool-docs.com/naviance/latest/release-notes-2026).

**Privacy and minors.** PowerSchool distinguishes school-directed processing from publicly accessible products. ActiveMatch shares identified data with institutions only on express consent; school-enabled Work Based Learning applies to students 13+ and involves permission before minimal information reaches an organization. Families should therefore understand both the school's agreement and the feature-specific sharing choice. These are vendor policy statements, not an independent compliance audit. [Global Privacy Statement](https://www1.powerschool.com/privacy/global-privacy-statement/).

**Lesson for this guide:** preserve an editable “must-have / nice-to-have” explanation and a single next step, without reproducing the school administration workflow.

## Xello

**Assessment and explanation.** Xello says answers are correlated with career activities, weighting both student preferences and how central an activity is to a career. Its second phase uses the Holland Model; the third refines matches. This is more explanatory than an unexplained top-career list. [Interests Assessments](https://help.xello.world/en-us/Content/Knowledge-Base/Xello-6-12/Assessments/Interests-Assessments.htm). Separate Skills Lab asks how frequently students want to use skills (35 questions/~10 minutes), rather than objectively testing proficiency; Learning Style is 20/~5. Published times distinguish on-task time from longer instructional time. [List of tasks in Xello 6–12](https://help.xello.world/en-us/Content/Knowledge-Base/Xello-6-12/Completion-Standards/List-of-Tasks.htm).

**Breadth and actions.** The official gallery documents college majors, graduate employment/salary, cost calculators, deadlines, applications, and scholarship features, alongside career research. Xello also advertises nine postsecondary pathways. [Features Gallery](https://xello.world/en/features-gallery/), [Career Exploration & Development](https://xello.world/en/career-exploration-development/). Goals, plans, a To do list, and educator completion tracking are documented; The Real Game simulates careers, education, expenses, and student loans. These provide a stronger lifestyle-planning reference than salary alone. [List of tasks in Xello 6–12](https://help.xello.world/en-us/Content/Knowledge-Base/Xello-6-12/Completion-Standards/List-of-Tasks.htm).

**UX and trust.** Staging gives value before completion of the full interest sequence. Vendor documentation says it works on mobile, tablet, and desktop; no responsive-session test was conducted. Public pages examined did not establish an assessment recalibration cadence, outcome validation, or a field-level occupation-data refresh schedule. [Features Gallery](https://xello.world/en/features-gallery/). Framework alignment should not be presented as proof of career destiny.

**Privacy and minors.** The policy says students cannot independently create accounts; schools/educators provision them and school-directed educators access student content. Xello says it does not sell/rent student information, does not use third-party advertising cookies in school/student services, and relies on schools for required under-13 parental consent. Requests to alter/delete school-provided information may go through the institution. [Xello Privacy Policy](https://xello.world/en-ca/privacy/).

**Lesson for this guide:** borrow staged refinement and visible answer-to-career reasons. Do not make a fixed “learning style” a gatekeeper for education or careers merely because competitors include one.

## Scoir

**Assessment and explanation.** Scoir's short interest assessment uses activity like/dislike responses and then filters career matches. It requires one sitting, does not save progress, and revisiting an earlier question requires resubmitting intervening answers. These are documented interaction costs despite the five-minute estimate. [Taking a career interest assessment](https://help.scoir.com/article/ss5linxlbo-taking-a-career-assessment). PrinciplesYou supplies archetypes and personality tendencies with a downloadable report; it can be resumed. [Discover Careers with PrinciplesYou](https://www.scoir.com/blog/for-students-discover-careers-with-principlesyou). Public documentation reviewed did not disclose the internal interest-scoring formula or per-answer contribution explanations.

**Breadth and actions.** Careers show income, education levels from high-school diploma through doctoral degree, outlook, requirements, and related general/specific majors leading into college search. Bright Outlook is attributed to O*NET. This verifies non-degree education filtering, rather than a complete apprenticeship-vacancy directory. [Discover careers](https://help.scoir.com/article/ba8f1xk0lq-discover-careers). My Colleges tracks stages, deadlines, checklists, document status, and activity history; some school-connected features depend on counselor settings. [My Colleges](https://help.scoir.com/article/eo07vpqsvt-my-colleges). Family financial estimates can use additional household inputs. [Getting Started as a Parent or Guardian](https://www.scoir.com/hubfs/Scoir%20Guide-%20Getting%20Started%20as%20a%20Parent%20or%20Guardian.pdf?hsLang=en-us). A lifestyle budget simulation was not verified.

**UX and accuracy.** Free independent access and a mobile app reduce the school-contract barrier. [Student and Family Pricing](https://www.scoir.com/students-families/pricing). Current Admission Intelligence marketing describes predictions using de-identified outcome records and similar student/high-school profiles; public calibration metrics and subgroup error rates were not verified. [Admission Intelligence](https://www.scoir.com/high-schools/admission-intelligence). Scattergram data depends substantially on alumni reporting outcomes; this is different from occupation-data freshness. [Managing and using Scattergrams](https://help.scoir.com/article/9dstwx6bb4-using-scattergrams-to-assess-admissions-probability). A universal college/career refresh cadence was not established.

**Privacy and minors.** Scoir's policy distinguishes school-administered processor roles from direct-account controller roles. Student-directed college contact sharing is documented; authenticated surfaces exclude advertising cookies, and session replay is disabled by default for school-administered student users. US under-13 accounts require parental or school authorization; EU under-16 use requires parental consent in the terms. Avoid reading a marketing “no sharing” slogan as excluding all authorized operational sharing. [Privacy and Legal Policies](https://www.scoir.com/terms-of-service).

**Lesson for this guide:** a short assessment is already competitive table stakes. Saving progress, editing any answer directly, and using plain-language reasons can differentiate the experience without increasing length.

## Unifrog

**Assessment and validation.** Interests uses Holland; Personality draws on Myers-Briggs theory; Work environments uses O*NET work contexts; Skills asks for self-evaluation of 22 skills. Separate numeracy, verbal-reasoning, and pattern-reasoning tests add assessed performance. Unifrog recommends Interests/Skills from 12, Work environments from 14, and Personality/Skills tests from 16. It recommends retakes about every 18 months and spacing quizzes rather than doing all at once. It discloses six-month quiz reviews, Cronbach's alpha/internal-consistency checks, year-group comparisons for Skills, and reviews of matching suggestions. This is unusually explicit process evidence; no published coefficients, subgroup calibration table, or longitudinal career-outcome validation was verified here. [Psychometric testing FAQs](https://www.unifrog.org/help/unifrogs-psychometric-testing-faqs).

**Breadth and actions.** UK apprenticeships/FE coexist with international university search and application work. [About Unifrog](https://www.unifrog.org/about). Its Gatsby documentation describes UK local/national median salaries, career and subject libraries, placements, opportunities including scholarships, student records, action plans, reminders, and adviser/parent involvement. UK labor-market coverage should not be assumed equivalent to localized US salary or trade information. [Unifrog and the Gatsby Benchmarks](https://cdn.unifrog.org/downloads/Unifrog_and_the_Gatsby_Benchmarks.pdf). Exact US cost-comparison or household lifestyle-budget capabilities were not verified.

**UX and freshness.** Module-by-module use fits optional depth, but multiple quizzes and school/account setup add possible complexity. No hands-on mobile findings are available. Unifrog names multiple institutional/government data sources and specifically says apprenticeship vacancies update nightly. That cadence applies to vacancies; it should not be generalized to all university fees, salary fields, or assessments. [About Unifrog](https://www.unifrog.org/about).

**Privacy and minors.** School agreements govern platform access; schools may invite parent accounts. The policy lists substantial academic, activity, and guidance data. It describes sharing selected student interactions with opted-in parents unless the student tells the school they prefer otherwise. The company says students see an easier-to-understand privacy version in line with the Children's Code. [Privacy Policy](https://www.unifrog.org/privacy-policy), [About Unifrog](https://www.unifrog.org/about). The practical lesson is to make who sees reflections explicit, rather than assuming parent access should reveal everything.

**Lesson for this guide:** make deeper modules separately named and timed. Treat the combination of interests, work context, and short real-world activities as exploratory evidence that can change.

## MajorClarity by Edmentum

**Assessment and matching.** The vendor describes combining personality/learning-style assessments, academic history, and exploration data into evolving career “fit scores.” Career test-drives add interactive activities and professional interviews. Inputs are disclosed at a high level; exact weights, item-level explanations, and calibration were not established. Its engagement and aligned-course-plan claims are vendor outcome claims, not evidence that each career recommendation is accurate. [Career Readiness](https://majorclarity.com/how-it-works/career-readiness), [MajorClarity at Edmentum](https://www.edmentum.com/products/major-clarity/).

**Breadth and actions.** Four-/six-year academic plans align with district courses and graduation requirements. Postsecondary tools include colleges/technical schools, scholarships, local-employer work-based learning, micro-credentials, applications, and transcripts. [MajorClarity at Edmentum](https://www.edmentum.com/products/major-clarity/). Institution pages document costs, offered programs, graduation rates, demographics, and scattergrams; side-by-side comparison and deadline/status tracking are included. [College Readiness](https://majorclarity.com/how-it-works/college-readiness). Standard salary/local labor-market detail and lifestyle budgeting were not confirmed in the examined current official pages.

**UX and data limits.** Test-drives are an appealing alternative to asking more introspective questions. Actual length, accessibility, mobile responsiveness, and when students first receive usable results remain untested. Current official assessment counts/times and a college/labor-data refresh schedule were not verified. The help entry point redirected to an Edmentum portal that did not expose the needed article content in this research session. [MajorClarity support entry point](https://support.majorclarity.com/hc/en-us).

**Privacy and minors.** The current site points to Edmentum; its website policy explicitly distinguishes educational-product privacy. The product policy says personal information is not sold/rented and educational profiling is restricted to customer educational purposes. Under-13 institutional access relies on school authority; direct/non-school institutional use requires parental consent. A legacy MajorClarity policy remains public, so procurement should establish the governing contract/policy version. [Edmentum Privacy Policy](https://www.edmentum.com/privacy-policy/), [Product Privacy Policy](https://www.edmentum.com/product-privacy-policy), [Legacy MajorClarity Privacy Policy](https://majorclarity.com/privacy-policy).

**Lesson for this guide:** after a few questions, offer a small “try this” activity and record the student's reaction. That can add useful evidence without building a longer survey.

## BigFuture by College Board

**Assessment and matching.** The Career Quiz uses the O*NET interest instrument, developed for the US Department of Labor, with ten activity-preference questions for each of six interest traits. Results give 30 career suggestions. These are interest matches, not objective aptitude scores or guaranteed careers. [What is the career quiz?](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/help-center/what-career-quiz). Career Search attributes data to Lightcast and O*NET and displays pay, growth, and recommended education. [Explore Career Possibilities](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/explore-careers). A published consumer-facing per-answer scoring breakdown was not verified.

**Breadth and actions.** The free resource covers four-year, community-college, and career-training pathways. Its major directory includes construction trades such as electrician, plumbing, welding, and HVAC. [Your Future, Your Way](https://information.collegeboard.org/your-future-your-way), [Majors Directory](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/majors). College/scholarship lists, financial-aid information, checklists, and net-price calculators support planning and affordability. [Personalizing Tools to Drive Student Success](https://allaccess.collegeboard.org/whats-next-bigfuture-personalizing-tools-drive-student-success). Household lifestyle simulation was not established.

**UX and freshness.** The public homepage visibly promotes a dashboard, profile completion, quizzes, recruitment, and scholarships. This verifies multiple entry points and setup prompts; it does not prove students find them confusing. [BigFuture Home](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/). College profile management distinguishes year-round updates from annual institutional survey submissions. Career-data ingestion cadence and product-specific matching calibration were not verified. [BigFuture Profile Management](https://highered.collegeboard.org/recruitment-admissions/bigfuture-profile-management).

**Mobile and minors.** BigFuture School is a separate free app, not universal mobile access to every web feature. Its July 30, 2026 policy permits access for eligible US school-day SAT Suite participants and/or AP students under school/state agreements, age 13+. [BigFuture School Use and Privacy](https://privacy.collegeboard.org/program-specific-privacy-policies/bigfuture-school-app-privacy-policy). The main privacy statement says online programs are for 13+ and some personalized tools require a student account. Voluntary Student Search Service shares specified identity/contact, academic-range, and planning information with participating educational organizations after opt-in; it can be opted out of. [Privacy Statement](https://privacy.collegeboard.org/privacy-statement), [Student Search Service](https://privacy.collegeboard.org/program-specific-privacy-policies/bigfuture/student-search-service).

**Lesson for this guide:** link out to trustworthy college/aid details while keeping the initial interaction focused. Recruiting consent should be separate from obtaining guidance.

## Cialfo

**Assessment and explanation.** May 29, 2026 help documentation names Human eSources' AchieveWorks Personality, Learning & Productivity, and Intelligences, counselor assignment, and Pro access. Do not assume every Cialfo contract includes every assessment. [Assessments on Cialfo](https://help.cialfo.co/en/articles/3694850-assessments-on-cialfo). Provider brochures describe personality preference codes, learning/productivity preferences, and multiple/emotional intelligences. Human eSources describes mapping assessment data to occupation attributes and “Compare to Me”; whether every provider report capability is exposed identically within Cialfo was not tested. [Personality brochure](https://assets.humanesources.com/materials/FlyerFeatures-AchieveWORKS-Personality.pdf), [Learning & Productivity brochure](https://assets.humanesources.com/materials/FlyerFeatures-AchieveWORKS-LearnProd.pdf), [Intelligences brochure](https://assets.humanesources.com/materials/FlyerFeatures-AchieveWORKS-Intelligences.pdf).

**Breadth and actions.** Cialfo emphasizes international university/program discovery, college lists, applications, counselor/parent workflows, and tasks. [What is Cialfo?](https://www.cialfo.co/what-is-cialfo). Current product updates describe separate Cost & Financial Aid, Courses & Majors, Scholarships, and Student Life sections. [Product Updates](https://help.cialfo.co/en/articles/5736506-product-updates). A comparable trade/apprenticeship catalog, local wage explorer, and lifestyle simulator were not verified. Its homepage describes Saige AI recommendations and task prioritization; no reproducible model specification or calibration table was found in the examined pages. [Cialfo Home](https://www.cialfo.co/).

**UX and freshness.** Published instructions say assessments are incompatible with the Cialfo mobile app and require desktop. Safari Mac/iPad instructions include temporarily disabling “Prevent Cross-Site Tracking” for assessments. That is a documented integration/privacy friction, distinct from a hands-on observed failure. [Assessments on Cialfo](https://help.cialfo.co/en/articles/3694850-assessments-on-cialfo). Product-release history establishes ongoing changes, but report-refresh intervals must not be mistaken for college-profile or labor-data refresh intervals. A universal content cadence and assessment outcome-validation study were not verified. [Product Updates](https://help.cialfo.co/en/articles/5736506-product-updates).

**Privacy and minors.** Cialfo's policy explicitly distinguishes processing for schools from controller activity for direct services. It describes student profiling and marketing purposes and says school-directed processing instead follows school agreements/policies. It is not intended for under-13 children. These separate roles matter when a family moves from school counseling features to direct or recruitment services. [Privacy Policy](https://www.cialfo.co/privacy-policy).

**Lesson for this guide:** simple conversational AI alone is not an unexplored advantage. A more defensible advantage is transparent reasons, fewer dependencies, and genuinely usable phone-first guidance.

## Adjacent family competitors

**Appily:** free for students, families, counselors, and schools; official tools include college/major quizzes, college planning, scholarships, and cost comparisons. Its college quiz collects academic interests, preferences, goals, and budget rather than testing aptitude; current exact item count/time was not verified. [Counselor FAQs](https://www.appily.com/guidance/counselors/faq), [College Match Quiz](https://www.appily.com/tools-quizzes/find-the-perfect-college). The FAQ describes matching via GPA/test scores/location and improving profiles, while explicitly acknowledging sharing with colleges, scholarship administrators, EAB, employers, marketing partners, and advertisers; the site identifies Appily as a data broker. These are material distinctions from a private family guide. The separately named Appily Match profile is described as 30 minutes; that is not the College Match Quiz duration. [Counselor FAQs](https://www.appily.com/guidance/counselors/faq). A public validation/refresh schedule was not established.

**Niche:** a close simplicity reference. Its free Major & Career Quiz advertises about five minutes and connects interests/self-reported strengths to majors, careers, and colleges. [College Major & Career Quiz](https://www.niche.com/college-majors-career-quiz/). Its College Quiz combines grades/scores with weighted priorities including academics, social life, safety, surroundings, and financial value, using data and reviews. No exact scoring formula or current calibration results were verified. [College Quiz](https://www.niche.com/colleges/college-quiz/). The 2026 privacy policy allows advertising/analytics disclosures, describes some disclosures as sale/sharing, and requires users under majority but at least 13 to have parental permission; under-13 use is prohibited. [Privacy Policy](https://www.niche.com/about/privacy/). Mobile/privacy protections should be checked by actual surface rather than inferred from the friendly landing page.

**CollegeVine:** materially relevant to admission probability and action-oriented explanations, rather than core career aptitude. Its free calculator names coursework, GPA, extracurriculars, intended major, rank, optional scores, and demographic inputs; colleges pay for ecosystem participation, and its landing page describes student-initiated sharing. [Admissions Calculator](https://www.collegevine.com/admissions-calculator/). A 2021 vendor article publishes aggregate calibration examples, including 50% predicted versus 48.1% admitted, and identifies the model as machine learning. This is historical vendor evidence, not a 2026 independent audit or a guarantee for an individual. [Is CollegeVine's Chancing Engine Actually Accurate?](https://blog.collegevine.com/is-collegevine-chancing-accurate). Current terms require age 13+ and parent/guardian agreement for minors. [Terms and Conditions](https://www.collegevine.com/legal/terms-and-conditions). Current detailed subgroup calibration, exact profile-completion burden, and feature parity on mobile remain unverified.

## Product recommendations for a short friendly guide

These are design judgments drawn from the comparison, not claims that a competitor lacks the proposed capability.

1. **Deliver initial value in a small first session.** Aim for roughly 8–12 conversational prompts and a clearly stated 3–5-minute expectation, validated with real teenagers. This is a product target, not a claim that a shortened instrument inherits the validity of a longer inventory. Allow skipping, “not sure,” direct editing, and automatic local progress saving.
2. **Show a few possibilities with reasons.** Start with three contrasting career/major families, each with two concrete reasons from the student's answers and one unresolved question. Make “why this fits” and “what might not fit” expandable. Keep every choice provisional and editable.
3. **Separate preference from preparedness and feasibility.** Label interests, work-context preferences, self-reported confidence, demonstrated skills, training requirements, affordability, and admission competitiveness separately. Do not turn school grades, personality type, or salary preference into a career ceiling.
4. **Offer depth only when it changes a decision.** Optional modules can cover work environment, everyday lifestyle, financial constraints, or a short activity. Show each module's time before starting. Let the student explore results without finishing them all.
5. **Connect each possibility to routes.** Show degree, community-college, certificate, apprenticeship, and employment routes where applicable. Put duration, typical education cost, location, wage range, work setting, and data date behind one “compare routes” control; distinguish sticker cost, net-price estimate, and household budget.
6. **Convert reflection into one small action.** Offer a career video, a sample task, a conversation with an adviser, or comparing two programs. Save the student's reaction as new evidence. Keep a three-item plan with dates and simple completion, rather than adopting a full counselor caseload system.
7. **Make trust inspectable.** For factual cards show source, geography, reference year, last retrieval, and uncertainty. Distinguish externally refreshed content from assessment model/version. Test answer stability, completion/drop-off, recommendation diversity, and usefulness across age/background groups; do not claim validity based solely on a RIASEC label.
8. **Design sharing around teen agency.** Start with private reflections. Make student/parent views explicit, offer a shareable discussion summary, and request separate, granular permission before any school/college/recruiter connection. Provide understandable deletion/export options and a clearly defined age/consent path before collecting identifying student data.

## Strongest limitations

- No authenticated school/family sessions were tested. Navigation burden, actual completion time, accessibility, and mobile quality need task-based testing with authorized demo access.
- Package and school configuration can change availability. Published school feature menus are not evidence that every student sees or must complete them.
- Publicly named frameworks and content providers do not establish individual prediction accuracy. Unifrog discloses a review process; CollegeVine provides historical vendor calibration; neither substitutes for a current independent outcome study across these products.
- General school-contract pricing was not verified. Free family access is specifically verified for Scoir, BigFuture, and Appily; promotional or geographically limited procurement prices were not generalized.
- Data maintenance is field-specific: nightly apprenticeship vacancies, annual institution surveys, product releases, SIS syncs, and hourly reports describe different update processes. Unknown ingestion dates remain unknown.
- No claim of feature absence should be inferred from a feature being unverified in public documentation.
